source_text: Magnum de modico malum scorpios terra suppurat: tot venena, quot genera; tot pernicies, quot et species; tot dolores, quot et colores, Nicander scribit et pingit: et tamen unus omnium violentiae gestus nocere de cauda; quae cauda erit, quodcumque de postumo corporis propagatur, et verberat. Proinde scorpii series illa nodorum, venenata intrinsecus venula subtilis, arcuato impetu surgens, hamatile spiculum in summo tormenti ratione stringit; unde et bellicam machinam, retractu tela vegetantem, de scorpio nominant. Id spiculum, et fistula est, patula tenuitate in vulnus et virus, qua figit effundit. Familiare periculi tempus aestas; Austro et Africo saevitia velificat. In remediis naturalia plurima; aliquid et magia circumligat, medicina cum ferro et poculo occurrit. Nam et praebibunt quidam, festinando tutelam; sed concubitus exhaurit, et denuo sitiunt. Nobis fides praesidium, si non et ipsa percutitur diffidentia signandi statim et adjurandi, et urgendi bestiae calcem: hoc denique modo etiam ethnicis saepe subvenimus; donati a Deo ea potestate, quam Apostolus dedicavit, cum morsum viperae sprevit. Quid ergo promittit stylus iste, si fides de suo tuta est? Ut et alias de suo tuta sit, cum suos scorpios patitur. Acerba mediocritas et istis, et genus varium, et uno modo armantur, et certo tempore subornantur, nec alio quam ardoris. Hoc apud Christianos persecutio est. Cum igitur fides aestuat, et Ecclesia exuritur de figura rubi, tunc Gnostici erumpunt, tunc Valentiniani proserpunt, tunc omnes martyriorum refragatores ebulliunt, calentes et ipsi offendere, figere, occidere. Nam quod sciant multos simplices ac rudes, tum infirmos, plerosque vero in ventum, et si placuerit, christianos, nunquam magis adeundos sapiunt, quam cum aditus animae formido laxavit; praesertim cum aliqua atrocitas fidem martyrum coronavit. Itaque primo trahentes adhuc caudam de affectibus applicant, aut quasi in vacuum flagellant. Haeccine pati homines innocentes? ut putes fratrem, aut de melioribus ethnicum? Siccine tractari sectam nemini molestam? Dehinc adigunt, perire homines sine caussa. Perire enim, et sine caussa, prima fixura. Exinde jam caedunt. Sed nesciunt simplices animae, quid, quomodo scriptum sit, ubi, et quando, et coram quibus confitendum, nisi quod nec simplicitas ista, sed vanitas, imo dementia, pro Deo mori. Et: Quis me salvum faciat, si is occidet, qui salvum facere debebit? Semel Christus pro nobis obiit, semel occisus est ne occideremur. Si vicem repetit, nunc et ille salutem de mea nece exspectat? An Deus hominum mundi sanguinem flagitat, maxime si taurorum et hircorum recusat? Certe peccatoris poenitentiam mavult quam mortem. Et quomodo non peccatorum desiderat mortem? Haec, et si qua alia admenta haereticorum venenorum, quem non vel in scrupulum figant, si non in exitium? vel in bilem, si non in mortem? At tu, fides si vigilat, ibidem scorpio pro solea anathema illidito, et relinquito in suo sopore morientem. Caeterum, si plagam satiaverit, intimat virus, et properat in viscera; statim omnes pristini sensus retorpescunt, sanguis animi gelascit, carne spiritus exolescit, nausea nominis inaccrescit. Jam et ipsa mens sibi quo vomat quaerit. Atque ita semel infirmitas quae percussa est, sauciatam fidem vel in haeresim, vel in saeculum exspirat. Et nunc praesentia rerum est medius ardor ipsa canicula persecutionis: ab ipso scilicet cynocephalo. Alios ignis, alios gladius, alios bestiae Christianos probaverunt. Alii fustibus interim et ungulis insuper degustata martyria in carcere esuriunt. Nos ipsi ut lepores, destinata venatio, de longinquo obsidemur, et haeretici ex more grassantur. Itaque tempus admonuit adversus nostrates bestiolas (promptam) mederi theriacam stylo temperare; qui legeris, biberis. Non amarum potio. Si eloquia Domini dulcia super mella et favos, inde pigmenta sunt; si lacte et melle promissio Dei manat, hoc sapiunt quae illuc faciunt. Vae autem qui dulce in amarum, et lumen in tenebras convertunt. Perinde enim et qui martyriis refragantur, salutem perditionem interpretantes, tam dulce in amarum, quam lucem in tenebras reformant, atque ita miserrimam hanc vitam illi beatissimae praevertendo, tam amarum pro dulci, quam tenebras pro luce supponunt.
pass_a_gloss: A great evil from a small thing, the scorpion of the earth suppurates: as many poisons, as many kinds; as many destructions, as many species; as many pains, as many colors, Nicander writes and depicts: and yet one gesture of violence of all harms from the tail; which tail will be, whatever is propagated from the last part of the body, and strikes. Therefore, that series of nodes of the scorpion, a poisonous little vein inside, rising with a curved impulse, binds a barbed dart at the top of the torment with reason; whence also a war machine, retracting projectiles, is named from the scorpion. That dart is also a pipe, with a wide thinness into the wound and the poison, with which it strikes and pours out. A familiar time of danger is summer; the south wind and the African wind make it savage. In remedies, there are many natural things; also magic binds something, medicine occurs with iron and a cup. For some also drink beforehand, hastening protection; but intercourse exhausts, and they thirst again. For us, faith is a protection, if not also it itself is struck by diffidence of signing immediately and adjuring, and urging the heel of the beast: in this way, finally, we also often help the gentiles; given by God that power, which the Apostle dedicated, when he despised the bite of a viper. What, therefore, does that style promise, if faith is safe from its own? So that also in other things it may be safe from its own, when it suffers its own scorpions. A bitter mediocrity is also for these, and a varied kind, and they are armed in one way, and they are prepared at a certain time, and not otherwise than with ardor. This is persecution among Christians. When, therefore, faith is boiling, and the Church is being burned from the figure of a ruby, then the Gnostics burst forth, then the Valentinians break out, then all the refusers of martyrdom boil over, being hot also to offend, to strike, to kill. For they know that many simple and unskilled people, then the weak, and for the most part those in the wind, and if it pleases, Christians, are never more to be approached, than when the fear of the soul has loosened the approach; especially when some atrocity has crowned the faith of martyrs. And so at first, still drawing the tail from the affections, they apply, or as if they flagellate in a vacuum. Is this to be suffered by innocent people? So that you might think a brother, or one of the better gentiles? Is a sect that bothers no one to be treated thus? Then they drive people to perish without cause. For to perish, and without cause, is the first fixing. From then on, they now strike. But the simple souls do not know what, how, and when, and before whom it is to be confessed, unless that not simplicity, but vanity, or rather madness, is to die for God. And: Who will save me, if he who ought to save me kills me? Christ died once for us, was killed once so that we might not be killed. If he repeats the turn, now also he expects salvation from my death? Or does God demand the blood of men of the world, especially if he refuses that of bulls and goats? Certainly, he prefers the repentance of a sinner to death. And how does he not desire the death of sins? These things, and if there are any other ravings of the poisons of heretics, do they not fix anyone either in doubt or in destruction? Or in bile, if not in death? But you, if faith is watchful, there the scorpion is struck with a sole, and the anathema is left in its own sleep, dying. Moreover, if it has satisfied the blow, it announces the poison, and hastens into the viscera; immediately all the former senses are restored, the blood of the soul grows cold, the spirit of the flesh grows weak, the nausea of the name increases. Now also the mind itself seeks what it may vomit. And so once the infirmity that was struck, the wounded faith breathes out either into heresy or into the world. And now the present things are the middle ardor, the very dog days of persecution: from the very cynocephalus. Others have tested Christians with fire, others with the sword, others with beasts. Others have tasted martyrdom in prison, and are dying of hunger, also with fustigations and nails. We ourselves, like hares, are destined for the hunt, and are besieged from afar, and the heretics are raging according to custom. And so the time has warned us to heal against our little beasts with a tempered style of theriac; you who read, drink. The drink is not bitter. If the words of the Lord are sweeter than honey and honeycombs, then they are pigments; if the promise of God flows with milk and honey, they taste what they make. Woe, however, to those who convert sweet into bitter, and light into darkness. For just as those who refuse martyrdom, interpreting salvation as perdition, reform sweet into bitter, and light into darkness, and thus pervert this most wretched life for the blessed one, they substitute bitter for sweet, and darkness for light.
pass_b_english: A massive evil oozes from something tiny: the scorpion of the earth. Nicander writes and paints it— as many poisons as kinds, as many destructions as species, as many pains as colors— yet only one gesture of violence from the tail does the harm. That tail is whatever extends from the body's rear, and it strikes. So the scorpion's segmented series, a poisonous internal vein rising on a curved impulse, locks a barbed dart at the summit of torment with mechanical precision; hence a siege engine that snaps back to launch its projectile takes its name from the scorpion. That dart is also a hollow tube, its wide thinness opening into the wound and the venom; with it the creature stabs and injects. Summer is the familiar season of danger; the south wind and the African wind whip the creature into savagery. Remedies abound in nature; magic also binds some; medicine meets the crisis with iron and cup. Some even drink beforehand, rushing protection; but intercourse exhausts them, and they thirst again. For us, faith is the shield— if it is not itself struck by the hesitation to sign, to adjure, to press the beast's heel immediately. In this way, finally, we often help even the gentiles; granted by God that power which the Apostle dedicated when he shrugged off the viper's bite (Acts 28:3-6). So what does this pen promise, if faith is safe on its own account? That it may be safe on its own account in other matters too, when it endures its own scorpions. A bitter mediocrity afflicts them as well, and a varied breed; they are armed in one way, recruited at a set time, and only by ardor. This is persecution among Christians. When faith boils, and the Church burns from the figure of the ruby, then the Gnostics burst forth, then the Valentinians break out, then all the refusers of martyrdom boil over, hot themselves to offend, to stab, to kill. For they know that many simple and unskilled people, then the weak, and for the most part those tossed on the wind, and if it pleases, Christians, are never more approachable than when fear has loosened the soul's defenses; especially when some atrocity has crowned the martyrs' faith. So at first, still drawing the tail from the affections, they apply it, or flail as if at empty air. Are innocent people to suffer this? So you might think a brother, or a better gentile? Is a sect that harms no one to be treated so? Then they drive people to perish without cause. For to perish, and without cause, is the first fixation. From then on they strike. But simple souls do not know what, how, where, when, or before whom to confess— unless not simplicity but vanity, rather madness, is to die for God. And: Who will save me, if the one who ought to save me kills me? Christ died once for us, was killed once so we would not be killed. If he demands a repeat, does he now expect salvation from my death? Or does God demand the blood of the world's men, especially when he refused that of bulls and goats? Certainly he prefers the sinner's repentance to death (Ezekiel 18:23). And how does he not desire the death of sins? These ravings of heretical poisons, and any others— do they not fix a person either in a scruple or in destruction? Or in bile, if not in death? But you, if faith watches, there strike the scorpion with a sandal, and leave the anathema dying in its own sleep. Moreover, if the blow is satisfied, the venom signals and rushes to the vitals; immediately all former senses go numb, the soul's blood freezes, the flesh's spirit dies out, nausea at the Name grows. Now the mind itself seeks something to vomit. And so the struck infirmity, the wounded faith, exhales either into heresy or into the world. And now the present reality is the middle ardor, the very dog days of persecution: from the dog-star itself. Fire tested some Christians, sword others, beasts others. Still others tasted martyrdom in prison and are starving, on top of beatings and nails. We ourselves, like hares, destined quarry, are besieged from afar, and heretics rage as usual. So the time has warned us to brew a theriac with a tempered pen against our little beasts; you who read, drink. The draught is not bitter. If the Lord's words are sweeter than honey and comb (Psalm 119:103), those are the pigments; if God's promise flows with milk and honey, they taste what they make. Woe to those who turn sweet to bitter, light to darkness. For just as those who refuse martyrdom, interpreting salvation as perdition, turn sweet to bitter and light to darkness, and thus pervert this most wretched life for the blessed one, they substitute bitter for sweet and darkness for light (1 Peter 2:20).
